subtitle: Queens, Cliffs and Temples: How Stone Made a Kingdom

panels.shot: epic wide of rocky cliffside at Bijolia, Jain temples crouched below, queen silhouetted above
panels.action: Chahamana Queen Rudrani stands in regal profile at the edge of Bijolia’s cliff, desert wind tugging her veil, as Jain temple spires and a sheer rock face fall away beneath her.

dialogue.text: On the cliff of Bijolia in the 12th century, queens and poets carved stone for Shaiva, Vaishnava and Jain alike—buying kingship not with swords, but with wells, temples and words.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी में बिजौलिया की चट्टान पर रानियों और कवियों ने शैव, वैष्णव और जैन सबके लिए पत्थर तराशा—राज तलवार से नहीं, कुओं, मंदिरों और शब्दों से खरीदा गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from harsh Rajasthani landscape to cluster of temples around Ajmer and Pushkar
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Aravalli hills reveals scattered shrines and lake-side temples around Ajmer and Pushkar under a hot, pale sky, with a royal palanquin in the distance.

dialogue.text: In Vigraharaja’s and Prithviraja’s time, Ajmer and Pushkar were more than frontier towns. They were a web of shrines and schools, where patronage meant power as surely as iron and cavalry.

i18n.hi: विग्रहराज और पृथ्वीराज के समय में अजमेर और पुष्कर सरहद नहीं, जाल थे–मंदिरों और पाठशालाओं के जाल, जहाँ सरपरस्ती ही लोहे और घुड़सवारों जितनी ताकत थी।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a palace hall, queen seated with brahmins and Jain elders, scrolls laid out
panels.action: Queen Rudrani sits upright on a low throne in a sandstone hall, listening as white-clad Jain elders and saffron-robed brahmins present palm-leaf manuscripts and temple plans.

dialogue.text: The Chahamana court knew this well. Shaiva ascetics, Vaishnava teachers and Jain elders all came to the queens’ chambers, asking not for armies, but for land, stone and the king’s name.

i18n.hi: चाहमान दरबार ये खेल समझता था। शैव साधु, वैष्णव गुरु और जैन आचार्य रानियों के कक्षों में आते, सेनाएँ नहीं, ज़मीन, पत्थर और राजा के नाम की मांग लेकर।

panels.shot: low-angle of Harshnath temple on a hill, solid against the sky
panels.action: The Harshnath temple crowns a hill, heavy stone pillars and carved lintels catching the evening light as villagers climb the path with offerings.

dialogue.text: On the high ridge of Harshnath in Sikar, a Shaiva temple rose under Chahamana hands. Its surviving pillars still carry their marks, proof that kingship was etched into the hilltop itself.

i18n.hi: सीकर के हर्षनाथ की ऊँची धार पर चाहमानों ने शैव मंदिर उठाया। बचे हुए स्तंभों पर आज भी उनके निशान हैं–सबूत कि राज ही पहाड़ी पर उकेरा गया था।

panels.shot: wide shot over Bisalpur lake, Bisaldeo temple at the edge, queen’s figure small near the steps
panels.action: By the waters of Bisalpur, the Bisaldeo temple stands at the shore, its plinth extending into the lake as Rudrani descends stone steps, touching the cool surface with her fingers.

dialogue.text: Beside the waters of Bisalpur, Vigraharaja’s Bisaldeo temple watched the lake. Such Shaiva shrines were not only holy; they anchored royal presence where water, trade and pilgrimage met.

i18n.hi: बिसालपुर के जल के किनारे विग्रहराज का बिसालदेव मंदिर झील पर नज़र रखता था। ऐसे शैव देवालय सिर्फ पवित्र नहीं थे, वे वहीं राज की मौजूदगी गाड़ देते जहाँ पानी, व्यापार और यात्रा मिलते।

panels.shot: close shot of Rudrani with an architect at Pushkar, pointing to a plan for lingam installations
panels.action: On the ghats of Pushkar, Rudrani stands with a temple architect, reviewing a palm-leaf sketch of Shiva shrines as priestly attendants gesture toward vacant niches along the lake.

dialogue.text: Jayanaka’s Prithviraja-Vijaya remembers queen Rudrani at Pushkar. It credits her with installing Shiva lingams around the sacred lake, weaving her name into the precinct’s stones.

i18n.hi: जयनाक के ‘पृथ्वीराज-विजय’ में पुष्कर की रानी रुद्राणी याद है। वह बताता है कि उसने पवित्र झील पर शिवलिंग बिठवाए, अपना नाम घाट-घाट की शिलाओं में पिरो दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot at Pushkar ghats, Rudrani offering instructions, masons at work in the background
panels.action: Rudrani, veiled but decisive, raises her hand as masons carve smooth lingam shafts on the steps and priests watch, the lake lying still behind them under the afternoon sun.

dialogue.speaker: the_chahamana_queens_and_court
dialogue.text: Place them where pilgrims rest. Let each journey end in worship and shade.

i18n.hi: उन्हें वहीं लगाओ जहाँ यात्री सुस्ता सकें। हर सफर का अंत हो पूजा और छाँव में।

panels.shot: wide shot of Pushkar temple zone with some shrines damaged, others repaired, workers moving
panels.action: Broken temple walls and toppled fragments lie beside newly repaired shrines at Pushkar, as Chahamana workers clear rubble and rebuild under the watchful eyes of Rudrani and priests.

dialogue.text: The same poem that praises Rudrani’s endowments also remembers Ghaznavid damage in Pushkar. In its verses, scarred precinct walls and new lingams stand side by side, in stone and memory.

i18n.hi: यही कविता जो रुद्राणी की देनदारी गाती है, पुष्कर में ग़ज़नवी तबाही भी याद रखती है। उसके श्लोकों में घायल घाट की दीवारें और नए लिंग, पत्थर और याद में साथ-साथ खड़े हैं।

panels.shot: intimate courtyard shot, another queen overseeing excavation of a deep stepwell near a shrine
panels.action: In a palace-adjacent courtyard, queen Somalekha watches laborers dig a deep, square shaft into the earth while, beyond them, a temple’s shikhara rises over the site.

dialogue.text: Jayanaka also names queen Somalekha. Before a temple, she ordered a stepwell sunk—water first, worship next—knowing that for a community, a shaded well could be holier than any battle.

i18n.hi: जयनाक रानी सोमलेखा का भी नाम लिखता है। मंदिर से पहले उसने बावड़ी खुदवाने का हुक्म दिया–पहले पानी, फिर पूजा–उसे मालूम था कि लोगों के लिए छायादार कुआँ किसी युद्ध से ज़्यादा पवित्र हो सकता है।

panels.shot: top-down shot looking into a finished stepwell, people drawing water, temple looming above
panels.action: Looking down into Somalekha’s finished stepwell, carved stairways spiral to clear water where villagers fill pots, while the temple tower rises above the well’s mouth in the background.

dialogue.speaker: the_chahamana_queens_and_court
dialogue.text: Let them speak of us when they drink, when they pray, when they teach.

i18n.hi: जब वे पानी पिएँ, जब वे पूजा करें, जब वे पढ़ाएँ–तब हमारा नाम बोलने दो।

panels.shot: medium shot in palace library, Rudrani listening to a court poet recite, scribes beside him
panels.action: In a lamp-lit hall, Rudrani listens as a court poet recites from a palm-leaf manuscript, while scribes to one side carefully trace Chahamana names and lineages onto new leaves.

dialogue.text: Kings fought. Queens endowed. Poets recorded. Between battles, the Chahamana world was stitched together by genealogies, waterworks and shrines, all carrying the dynasty’s claim.

i18n.hi: राजे लड़े। रानियाँ दान देती रहीं। कवि दर्ज करते रहे। युद्धों के बीच चाहमान संसार कुँडों, कुल-कथाओं और देवालयों के धागों से सिलता गया, हर धागे पर राजवंश का दावा।

panels.shot: dramatic shot of the Bijolia cliff face with carvers at work, Jain temple roofs below
panels.action: At Bijolia, stone carvers cling to scaffolds on a sheer cliff, chiseling lines of script into the rock, while the roofs of a Jain temple complex press close below the inscription site.

dialogue.text: In 1170, a long inscription was carved on Bijolia’s cliff beside Jain temples. Its letters proclaim Chahamana lineages and grants, facing the merchant and Jain world it sought to bind.

i18n.hi: ११७० में बिजौलिया की चट्टान पर जैन मंदिरों के पास लम्बी शिलालेख खुदी। उसके अक्षर चाहमान वंश और दानों का ऐलान करते हैं, उस व्यापारी और जैन जगत की ओर मुँह करके जिसे बाँधना था।

panels.shot: close-up of chisel and hand carving Nagari letters, tiny Jain shrine blurred behind
panels.action: A craftsman’s steady hand drives a chisel into stone, forming crisp Nagari letters while a small Jain shrine with its image hall stands out of focus in the background.

dialogue.text: That Bijolia rock inscription still survives. It speaks of grants, officials and dates, but its setting—beside Jain spires—shows who needed to read it: traders and temple communities.

i18n.hi: वो बिजौलिया शिला-लेख आज भी बचा है। उसमें दान, अफ़सर और तिथियाँ दर्ज हैं, पर उसका पड़ोस–जैन कलशों के बीच–बताता है कि किसे पढ़ना था: व्यापारी और मंदिर समाजों को।

panels.shot: wide interior of a Jain temple at Bijolia, Rudrani entering with attendants, merchants present
panels.action: Inside the cool hall of a Jain temple at Bijolia, Rudrani enters with a few attendants, hands folded, as local merchants and Jain monks stand respectfully beside carved columns.

dialogue.text: The same realm that raised Harshnath and Bisaldeo also endowed Jain institutions. Supporting many paths at once was strategy: each temple network carried its own followers and wealth.

i18n.hi: जिस राज ने हर्षनाथ और बिसालदेव उठाए, उसने जैन संस्थाएँ भी सँभालीं। कई मार्गों को साथ-साथ साधना एक चाल थी–हर मंदिर-समाज अपने लोग और अपना धन लेकर आता था।

panels.shot: balanced shot showing Shaiva shrine on one side, Jain temple on the other, queen in between
panels.action: On a ridge, a Shaiva shrine stands to one side and a Jain temple to the other, while Rudrani pauses between them, the wind lifting her veil as she looks from one spire to the next.

dialogue.text: Historians like Dasharatha Sharma trace this web of patronage. Shaiva, Vaishnava and Jain gifts did not cancel each other; together they widened the circle that a Chahamana king could claim.

i18n.hi: दशरथ शर्मा जैसे इतिहासकार इस सरपरस्ती के जाल का पीछा करते हैं। शैव, वैष्णव और जैन दान एक-दूसरे को नहीं काटते, साथ मिलकर उस घेरा को फैलाते हैं जिस पर चाहमान राजा दावा कर सके।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot showing stepwell, Pushkar ghats, Harshnath hill, Bijolia cliff in one frame
panels.action: A composite panorama blends Somalekha’s stepwell, Pushkar’s ghats with lingams, Harshnath’s hilltop temple and the Bijolia inscription cliff into a single sweeping, sunlit landscape.

dialogue.text: By the late 12th century, the Chahamana name was not only in war songs. It lived in wells that held water, temples that held gods, and inscriptions that held memory, across their scattered realm.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के अंत तक चाहमान नाम सिर्फ युद्ध-गीतों में नहीं था। वह उन कुओं में था जो पानी थामते, उन मंदिरों में जो देव थामते, और उन लेखों में जो याद थामते, पूरे बिखरे हुए राजभर।

panels.shot: introspective close-up of Rudrani, eyes lowered, temple bells faint in the background
panels.action: Rudrani sits quietly near a courtyard shrine, eyes lowered in thought as distant temple bells ring through the dusk and a mason’s silhouette passes by with tools on his shoulder.

dialogue.text: Today, soldiers’ names are louder than queens’ and builders’. Yet in Ajmer, Pushkar and Bijolia, it is their stones and wells that still stand, reminding us how power was really rooted in the land.

i18n.hi: आज सिपाहियों के नाम रानियों और गढ़इयों से ज़्यादा गूँजते हैं। पर अजमेर, पुष्कर और बिजौलिया में आज भी पत्थर और कुएँ खड़े हैं, याद दिलाते कि असली ताकत ज़मीन में कैसे जड़ पकड़े थी।

title_i18n.en: The Cliff of Bijolia and the Temples of Ajmer
title_i18n.hi: बिजौलिया की चट्टान और अजमेर के मंदिर

subtitle_i18n.en: Queens, Cliffs and Temples: How Stone Made a Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: रानियाँ, चट्टानें और मंदिर: पत्थर से बना राज
